chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from one of his men, who said:

I asked him about the limit concerning the mukārī who fasts and performs full prayer. He said: Any mukārī who stays in his home or in the town that he enters for less than ten days, fasting and full prayer are always obligatory upon him. But if his stay in his home or in the town that he enters is more than ten days, then shortening the prayer and breaking the fast apply to him.

key_terms.الصِّيَامُ: the obligatory fast in this legal context
key_terms.الْإِفْطَارُ: not fasting, i.e. breaking or leaving the fast during travel
key_terms.الْمُكَارِيِّ: a hired transporter or muleteer whose work involves repeated travel
key_terms.يُتِمُّ: performs the prayer in full rather than shortened form

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a mukārī regarding fasting and full or shortened prayer when staying less or more than ten days?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the mukārī and when he must observe fasting and full prayer versus shortened prayer and breaking the fast. The ruling turns on whether his stay in his home or in a town he enters is less than ten days or more than ten days.
